doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Civil rights era riots on tour
summary: The band encountered riots in Los Angeles, near Detroit and in Milwaukee.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: The years you were with him were pretty intense times for civil rights. Did that movement affect Ellington at all, or the operations of the band?

Well I don’t think it affected Ellington in his attitudes but I’m sure he had some thoughts about it because he had thoughts about everything. But we did run into a few riots. One, the one in L.A., we were playing at Disneyland and a riot broke out that night and they wouldn’t let us back to our places. We couldn’t get back there. Isn’t that amazing? We couldn’t go through certain sections of town. Things were burning. And once we were outside of Detroit and a similar thing happened. They wouldn’t let us in town. Mercer made the announcement. “They says we can’t stay in town tonight fellas, we’ll have to stay on the outskirts.” And once in Milwaukee we went in with an armed guard I believe, they escorted us through the thing there. They were having some problems. Those are the three cases that I remember.
